source.title: Reducing information dependency does not cause training data privacy. Adversarially non-robust features do
source.authors: Rasmus Torp; Shailen Smith; Adam Breuer

page_placements.theme: Training fit does not determine generalization or representation quality

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. The extracted text has some layout corruption in later sections, but the relevant results in Table 2 and Appendix A.3.1 are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains ResNet models with permuted labels and reports training and test accuracy, directly applying the random-label intervention and measurements relevant to V1 in new settings.
record.gate_note: The random-label results in Table 2 are the only results bearing on the claim versions. The paper also reports model-inversion metrics, but those do not measure the listed versions. The study cites Zhang et al. (2017); cited findings are not cataloged as its own results.
record.test_reason: Table 2 reports the study's own training and test accuracies after label randomization, directly testing V1's fitting result using the original intervention and measures on FaceScrub ResNets.
record.authors_conclusion: The record captures the authors' interpretation: despite 99.6% and 99.4% training accuracy on permuted labels, PPA reconstructions collapse, which they argue shows that rote memorization alone does not explain reconstruction leakage. Their broader conclusion concerns information dependency and non-robust features in high-resolution image classification.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the permuted-label intervention and training/test accuracy measures associated with the cited Zhang et al. setting, but evaluates FaceScrub ResNets in a model-inversion study and lowers the learning rate for permuted-label runs.
record.method_sensitivity: The permuted-label runs use a lower learning rate of 0.0001 than the general target-model setting of 0.001.

fits_no_version.finding: PPA reconstruction distance increases from 0.768 to 1.249 for ResNet-152 and from 0.781 to 1.251 for ResNet-18 after label permutation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Near-perfect fitting of randomized training labels can coexist with poor class-representative reconstruction by model inversion attacks.

record.problems: The random-label result uses a lowered learning rate, so it does not establish the unchanged-hyperparameters condition. Table 2 reports no uncertainty for its accuracy values.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant rows left out. Model-inversion L2-Face results in Table 2 do not measure the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: Fitting with unchanged training hyperparameters: the learning rate is reduced from 0.001 to 0.0001. The text describes randomized/permuted labels but does not specify the permutation procedure sufficiently to verify independent random labeling.
Relative time to convergence and changes in convergence speed across corruption fractions. A common 100-epoch budget does not measure either.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs to zero training error.
Training fit and steady test-error degradation across intermediate label-corruption fractions.
Comparisons establishing whether weight decay, dropout, or augmentation prevent random-label fitting, and whether removing regularization preserves true-label generalization.
Training trajectories establishing that shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict based solely on the changed learning rate: unchanged-hyperparameter fitting was not tested, and no failure at the original learning rate is reported. Label permutation is the claim's experimental intervention, rather than a separate training objective engineered to produce memorization. The text calls the labels randomized; permutation alone does not establish that the labels were insufficiently random.

versions.untested_parts: Tests permuted labels on FaceScrub using ResNet-152 and ResNet-18, reporting training and test accuracy. It does not use completely random labels as worded in the claim, and it lowers the learning rate to 0.0001 for the permuted-label runs; it does not establish fitting without changes to training hyperparameters.
